==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|stage}}, from {{der|en|fro|estage|t=dwelling, residence; position, situation, condition}}, from {{der|en|fro|ester|t=to be standing, be located}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|stæþþan|t=to make staid, stay}}, {{cog|non|steðja|t=to place, provide, confirm, allow}}, {{cog|ang|stede|t=state, status, standing, place, station, site}}. More at {{l|en|stead}}. {{doublet|en|étage}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/steɪd͡ʒ/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-stage.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-stage.wav|a=UK}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪdʒ|s=1}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A [[phase]]. #: {{ux|en|He is in the recovery '''stage''' of his illness.}} #: {{ux|en|Completion of an identifiable '''stage''' of maintenance such as removing an aircraft engine for repair or storage.}} #* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|chapter=1|passage=Such a polity is suited only to a particular '''stage''' in the progress of society.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1986|author=Daniel Woodrell|title=Under the Bright Lights|page=66 |passage="They're [[bikini briefs]]", Nicole said. "That just means sexy underwear."
"I though naked was sexy."
"Well, it is. But sexy comes in '''stages'''".}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=w:Donald Keene|title=Emperor of Japan: Meiji and His World, 1852-1912|url=https://archive.org/details/emperorofjapanme0000keen/|location=New York|publisher=w:Columbia University Press|ISBN=0-231-12340-X|OCLC=909761376|page=588|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/emperorofjapanme0000keen/page/588/ |text=The Russians had promised to withdraw in three '''stages'''. One '''stage''' had been completed, and the railway between Shan-hai-kwan and Ying-k’ou (Newchang) had been returned, but all this meant was that the Russians had moved their troops from Liao-hsi, a region where they had few interests, to their major base at Liaotung.}} # {{lb|en|by extension}} One of the portions of a device (such as a [[rocket]] or [[thermonuclear weapon]]) which are used or activated in a particular order, one after another. #: {{ux|en|The first '''stage''' of the launcher burned out and separated after successfully boosting the payload onto a suborbital trajectory, but the engine of the upper '''stage''' failed to ignite to place the satellite into orbit.}} # {{senseid|en|Q194428}}{{lb|en|theater}} A [[platform]]; a surface, generally [[elevated]], upon which show performances or other public events are given. #: {{ux|en|The band returned to the '''stage''' to play an [[encore]].}} #* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Criticism|passage=Knights, squires, and steeds must enter on the '''stage'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1829|author=w:Charles Sprague|title=Curiosity |passage=Lo! Where the '''stage''', the poor, degraded stage, / Holds its warped mirror to a gaping age.}} # A [[floor]] or [[storey]] of a house. # A floor elevated for the convenience of mechanical work, etc.; [[scaffolding]]; [[staging]]. # A [[platform]], often floating, serving as a kind of [[wharf]]. # {{senseid|en|Q339249}} A [[stagecoach#English:_Q339249|stagecoach]], an [[enclosed]] [[horsedrawn]] [[carriage]] used to carry passengers; the service that such coaches provide; a company that operates such service. #: {{ux|en|The '''stage''' pulled into town carrying the payroll for the mill and three ladies.}} #: {{ux|en|In the 1880s he ran a '''stage''' that connected various interior towns with the coastal port.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=April 14 1711|publisher=w:Jonathan Swift|title=[[s:The Works of the Rev. Jonathan Swift/Volume 15/Journal to Stella - Letter 21|letter]] to [[w:Esther Johnson|Stella]] |passage=I went in the sixpenny '''stage'''.}} #* {{RQ:Cowper Poems|Conversation |passage=a parcel sent you by the '''stage'''}} # {{senseid|en|place to rest during a journey; station for relay of horses}} {{lb|en|dated}} A place of rest on a regularly travelled road; a [[station]], [[way station]]; a place appointed for a [[relay#Noun|relay]] of horses. # {{lb|en|dated}} A degree of advancement in a journey; one of several portions into which a road or course is marked off; the distance between two places of rest on a road. #: {{ux|en|a '''stage''' of ten miles}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1807|author={{w|Francis Jeffrey, Lord Jeffrey|Francis Jeffrey}}|title=Clarkson on Quakerism|journal={{w|The Edinburgh Review}} April 1807 |passage=A '''stage''' {{...}} signifies a certain distance on a road.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1858|author=w:Samuel Smiles; w:Robert Stephenson|title=The Life of George Stephenson: Railway Engineer|url=http://books.google.com.au/books?id=PKOV67lbNMAC|page=356 |passage=He travelled by gig, with his wife, his favourite horse performing the journey by easy '''stages'''.}} #* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price| chapter=3| passage=The ''Mount Vernon'', favoured by a good '''stage''' of water, soon cleared the narrow Monongahela channel, passed the confluence, and headed down under full steam, […].}} # {{lb|en|electronics}} The number of an [[electronic]] [[circuit]]’s block, such as a filter, an amplifier, etc. #: {{ux|en|a 3-'''stage''' cascade of a 2nd-order bandpass Butterworth filter}} # The [[place]] on a [[microscope]] where the [[slide]] is [[locate]]d for viewing. #: {{ux|en|He placed the slide on the '''stage'''.}} # {{lb|en|video games}} A [[level]]; one of the areas making up the game. #: {{synonyms|en|level}} #: {{ux|en|How do you get past the flying creatures in the third '''stage'''?}} # A place where anything is publicly exhibited, or a remarkable affair occurs; the [[scene]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|IV|vi|passage=When we are born, we cry that we are come / To this '''stage''' of fools.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Poems|poem=Passion|page=16|passage=Ere while of Muſick, and Ethereal mirth,
Wherewith the '''ſtage''' of Ayr and Earth did ring,}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Gary Andres; Paul Hernnson|title=Lobbying Reconsidered: Politics Under the Influence|page=149 |passage=Paid media is the admission ticket to enter the big-time Washington '''stage'''.}} # {{senseid|en|geology}}{{lb|en|geology}} The [[w:Geologic record|succession of rock strata]] laid down in a single age on the [[geologic time scale]]. # {{lb|en|Canada|Quebec}} An [[internship]]. # The notional space within which [[stereo]] [[sound]]s are positioned, determining where they will appear to come from when played back. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=Roey Izhaki|title=Mixing Audio: Concepts, Practices and Tools|page=391 |passage=This way, we simply stretch the image of a monophonic sound across a wider area on the stereo '''stage''' and create an altogether bigger impression.}} # {{lb|en|metonym|uncountable|with "the"}} The [[profession]] of an [[actor]]. #* {{quote-book|en|author=[[w:W.
